title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: JOYCE'S CITY
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Joyce Pemberton, fifty-four, from Baltimore, Maryland.
For thirty-one years, she packed soap at the factory by the harbor.
Then one Friday, the factory closed for good.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE LAST WHISTLE
segments.quote: There are years that ask questions and years that answer.
segments.author: Zora Neale Hurston
lines: For a month, Joyce sat by the window in her robe, eating crab chips.
Her sister mailed her a book by Zora Neale Hurston, with one line circled:
There are years that ask questions and years that answer.
So Joyce got dressed, and went out to find some answers.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: LOST VISITORS
segments.quote: You've got to be very careful if you don't know where you're going, because you might not get there.
segments.author: Yogi Berra
lines: At the harbor, a family from Ohio was turning their map upside down.
Joyce pointed the way, then told them where her grandpa proposed, and where to get the best crab cake.
An hour later, the dad laughed and said, like Yogi Berra used to say,
You've got to be very careful if you don't know where you're going, because you might not get there.
He tried to pay her twenty dollars. That night, Joyce printed flyers.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: TWO CUSTOMERS
segments.quote: Few things are impossible to diligence and skill.
segments.author: Samuel Johnson
lines: Her first tour, two people came. Her cousin, and a man who thought it was the bathroom line.
Joyce almost quit. Then she found a line from Samuel Johnson, the English writer:
Few things are impossible to diligence and skill.
So she walked the route every morning, and showed up every Saturday.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE BORING PART
segments.quote: We tell ourselves stories in order to live.
segments.author: Joan Didion
lines: But her tours were stuffed with dates. One man fell asleep standing up.
Back home, Joyce opened a book by Joan Didion. The first line:
We tell ourselves stories in order to live.
So she tossed her note cards and told stories. The baker who burned the mayor's cake. The night the harbor froze. Nobody slept again.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE STORM
segments.quote: Don't knock the weather; nine-tenths of the people couldn't start a conversation if it didn't change once in a while.
segments.author: Kin Hubbard
lines: One August day, with twenty people on the tour, a thunderstorm rolled in.
Joyce ducked them into a tiny bar and remembered the humorist Kin Hubbard:
Don't knock the weather; nine-tenths of the people couldn't start a conversation if it didn't change once in a while.
So she asked about the worst storm back home. They talked for an hour, soaking wet. Five stars.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: EVERYBODY'S CITY
segments.quote: Cities have the capability of providing something for everybody, only because, and only when, they are created by everybody.
segments.author: Jane Jacobs
lines: By spring, Joyce had a waiting list. Her old coworkers still needed work.
On her fridge hung a line from Jane Jacobs, who wrote about cities:
Cities have the capability of providing something for everybody, only because, and only when, they are created by everybody.
So she trained three of them. Now each one tells the stories of their own block.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Ask. Find your way. Keep at it. Tell stories. Enjoy the rain. Bring everybody.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Ask the question. Know where you're going. Keep at it. Tell stories. Enjoy the rain. Bring everybody.
I once gave my wife a tour of our own house. She found the cookies I hid.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
